odd_even.verdict_text: The two dips are different sizes — odd transits dip 0.120% but even transits dip 0.340% (65% apart). That is the classic sign of an eclipsing binary whose real period is twice the candidate period.

double_period.verdict_text: The light between the eclipses is not flat — at the quarter-orbit points the system brightens to 1.0496 while the shoulders beside the eclipses sit at 1.0185: a 3.11% wave at 20σ. That brightening is two stars squeezed out of round by each other's gravity, showing us their wider sides twice per orbit — a planet is far too light to bend its star like this. These are twin stars orbiting every 27.10 days, not a planet.
